messages:
lia: noticed a customer (acme) escalation — they started getting 504s to hosted /v1/generate right after the canary at 13:17 UTC.
oncall-bot: incident CREATED INC-2347 — priority P1
maria: what's the error pattern? 504s across all routes or specific?
lia: looks like requests with large auth headers/timeouts. error rate ~12% on canary slice, baseline ~0.3% on stable.
devon: grabbing logs now. prefix search for acme client_id
devon: log sample: `ts=2026-03-07T13:18:02Z req_id=ab12 client=acme status=504 upstream=timeout backend=grpc_deadline_exceeded header_len=128 route=/v1/generate` — repeated
sam: header_len=128 stands out. our prod default is 4096. any header-sanitizer changes in the canary?
ia: we flipped header_sanitizer.max_header_bytes down in the new canary config to try to reduce memory pressure for streaming. probably scoped wrongly.
devon: confirmed in canary config: `routing.headers.sanitizer.max_bytes: 128` — that should have been a feature flag scoped to internal-only but got applied to default route template.
maria: that would cause long signed auth headers (ACME uses big JWTs with extra claims) to be truncated -> upstream auth service returns weird error and the gateway ends up waiting and timing out.
jordan-cs: customer says they see timeouts starting 13:17 UTC, they repro with a single curl containing long X-AUTH-PROPS header. asking for ETA.
devon: can reproduce locally, sending curl repro:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "X-AUTH-PROPS: <very-long-header....>" \
  -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
```
response: 504 after 15s with upstream timeout in logs.
sam: can we roll the canary back? which deploy owns the change?
devon: change was in deploy 2026-03-07T13:16 by pipeline `canary/edge-rolling/3`. I can initiate rollback to previous config.
lia: coordinate with oncall and cs: @jordan-cs tell customer we're rolling back and will follow up with root cause.
oncall-bot: runbook step: rollback canary route-config -> execute
devon: starting rollback now — `kubectl set configmap route-config canary=previous --namespace=prod` (running)
maria: checking metrics: request latency for canary slice trending down already? (watching)
devon: rollback applied. restart of edge pods in canary slice triggered.
sam: I see canary pods restarting, traffic rebalanced to stable.
lia: getting fresh logs: `req_id=ab12 status=200 upstream=ok header_len=4096` — looks fixed for the repro case.
jordan-cs: told customer rollback started, they reported improvement within ~2 minutes, now 200s on their repro.
maria: error rate on canary slice back to baseline. no billing impacts observed yet but flagged.
lia: creating follow-up ticket for config scoping + add a guard in pipeline to prevent route-default overrides without review.
devon: adding a unit test + lint to pipeline to ensure header_sanitizer changes require explicit opt-in. PR coming.
sam: recommend a short postmortem and a customer-facing note. lia, can you own the CS update?
lia: yes. I'll post summary in #customer-success and send acme the incident note. tagging for postmortem: @devon @maria @sam
oncall-bot: incident RESOLVED INC-2347 — rollback successful, monitoring for 30m
lia: closing thread here. thanks all :thumbsup:
